messages:
simon: Heads-up: seeing a burst of reconnects from mobile clients behind CDN-us-west. Pattern: upstream sends TCP RST (not FIN) after idle, client reconnects and issues full init -> user sessions doubled in our billing logs.

priya: RST? That's nasty. RST usually means TCP-level hard close (no graceful), clients can't resume. Do we know which hop sent it? edge or CDN?

joel: Trace shows L7 (cdn-edge-03) closed downstream conn due to perceived idle — but it used RST when the origin tcp keepalive hadn't fired. Logs: 
```
cdn-edge-03 | conn=0x7f9 idle=95s action=terminate reason=idle_timeout method=RST
origin-proxy | downstream received RST conn=0x7f9
server       | resume-token header=rt_abc123 present -> unable to resume (rst)
client       | reconnect -> new init rt_abc123
```

simon: Because it's RST the browser ws.onclose sees code=1006 (abnormal) and we fall back to full init flow. We do have resume semantics only when we observe graceful close or keepalive probe.

priya: Short-term mitigation idea: accept duplicate resume-token on init up to 45s and mark those in telemetry as reconnect.split. Longer-term: adjust CDN idle thresholds or change keepalive interval. Both have tradeoffs.

joel: Agree on telemetry. Add metric stream.reconnect.split and label by client.platform (ios/android/web). Grafana should show the spike overlayed with cdn-edge id.

infra-ci: Deployment job queued: joel/init-token-soft-accept -> canary us-west-2.

simon: UX/console note: operators currently see only total session count. We should annotate the Sessions dashboard with a checkbox to hide soft reconnects (reconnect.split) so customer-facing numbers exclude these transients. Priya can you file a console ticket?

priya: Filing: https://go/redwood/tickets/CONS-2041 - add session filter and add new alert. Proposed alert: stream.reconnect.split > 30/min for a region AND sustained for 5m. Pager to oncall.

joel: Implementation detail for soft-accept: on init, if resume-token present and we've seen a recent session with same token within window, then attach existing session instead of creating new one. Need to be careful with session state mutation and in-flight messages. Suggest idempotent-ack handshake: server returns header X-Resume-Accepted: true and resume-session-id.

simon: Good point. If we resume we must replay pending server events or reconcile last-ack seq. If we accept as new session due to RST we currently lose continuity. Soft-accept should try to reattach KV-cache and sequence index.

joel: I'll prototype with a read-only attach first (no state mutation) to avoid concurrency weirdness. If attach succeeds we flip to a full resume after verifying seq delta < 50.

infra-ci: Canary deployed to us-west-2, 3 nodes. Job: joel/init-token-soft-accept #build-4123

simon: Monitoring: added grafana panel for stream.reconnect.split + cdn-edge-id series. Also added dashboard alert rule preview.

joel: (3m) early canary: reconnect.split metric on canary nodes increased (expected) but total new-sessions dropped 78% vs baseline for the same clients. No CPU increase.

priya: Nice. Can we get mobile platform breakdown?

joel: (6m) breakdown: 85% iOS, 10% Android, 5% Web. Looks like iOS socket behavior + carrier / CDN interaction.

priya: Follow-ups: (1) console ticket for session filter & alert (CONS-2041) (2) CDN config task to increase idle threshold in us-west for mobile paths (ops-runbook) (3) RFC to formalize soft-attach semantics (joel to author).

simon: I'll draft runbook blurb for oncall: how to identify RST vs FIN, which dashboards to check, and rollback steps. Put a hint to correlate cdn-edge id and carrier.

joel: RFC link (draft): https://go/redwood/rfc/soft-attach-resume - notes about seq reconciliation and idempotency window defaults (45s).

priya: I'll add alert text and paging matrix. Suggest we page infra-team first then eng-platform if >3 regions affected.

infra-ci: CI note: rolling to full us-west after 30m green.

simon: Thanks. If anyone sees unexpected memory growth or event reorder issues, ping here. Closing thread after full roll completes.
